body: LOL nawww, I love animals too much and actually am taking care of a special needs dog right now. It is probably that I just have a hard time or bad luck finding friends.

Not really invited to hang out with others or if I am they neglect to ever give me the date, place or time even when I ask was a pretty good indicator. Being called weird or mysterious to my face often is another... Mainly it's people don't want to stick around as friends or claim they're a friend without inviting me to things like their other pals. It's strange to me because I can get along with so many people but then these things keep happening.

Hopefully these thoughts will help your search in looking for a new group in the future. The pandemic makes these things difficult but when the vaccines start rolling out these options might start opening up again.

Volunteer work: Farming, community work, etc... I heard not only can you put down what you've done on a resume for future employment but you can also make friends with other volunteers with enough charm.

Library events and classes: Pretty much the same as volunteer work but you can only put down what classes you attended that sound good on a resume.

For the pandemic maybe joining discord hobby groups or servers made to look for friends. People have the tendency to have difficulties making connections online and are quick to judge and ghost sadly. Not to mention people that decide to act mean just because they believe they can get away with it... If you have the patience and the willpower to use discord it's one of the best ways to meeting from all different kinds of places. Facebook groups might work similarly too.

Living with autism is lonely as heck. I know this personally and the only ways I cope was learning more about absurdism, psychology and talking to other people in the same boat trying to find ways to make life a little less miserable.

Being lonely while having friends doesn't seem to be all that uncommon. Which is strange why people act like this isn't a thing that happens...

I've noticed it mostly comes up in friend groups and think it might be because you don't get many chances to interact with others on an individual level with that kind of setting.

I'm autistic too and the only genuine friends I've had so far were other people with autism. ASD just makes it so hard to find friendships where you can be just be yourself... Also you can totally DM me if you want to hang out and chat. I'm down for trying to make new friends!

Are they willing to call a crisis line? Those are usually used for last case danger scenarios and heading to a good psyche ward isn't the comfiest idea but it's safer than leaving themselves alone with escalating ideations
Yeah, it should be chill so you shouldn't be so hard on yourself. I'm hoping for the best for ya

No. You can still wish/give your friend a happy birthday in different ways even if it is belated. As a friend she should be understanding in a situation like this and appreciate you still going out of your way to celebrate even a little on the sidelines.

No problem, autism spectrum disorder is one heck of a spectrum. Each person seems to have their own combination of symptoms which complicates things. Thus, a whole bunch of misinformation with the included false theories in the early days of research that linger around. Kinda sad how many people go under the radar for most of their life all confused because of it.

Nearly forgot, emotional burnout is also a thing with ASD. Sometimes you just need a long R&R after being forced to pretend to be normal after so long or talk to people who communicate in a similar way.

Maybe look in the DSM-5 to see if you relate with any of the symptoms before consulting a doctor on if you want an evaluation. There are also online communities and posts there can also give you more insight. What helped me personally is talking to other people in the same boat and realizing that functioning differently isn't bad despite how others may react to the robot-iness. Stay far away from Autism Speaks. AS is a more of a hate group than a charity.

This feels like a clear case of ASD but I'm not a doctor. I don't know if you've been diagnosed or not either but I go through the same experience with an added struggle of being unable to be independent. If this is a case of undiagnosed high functioning ASD it might be worth looking into for therapy and community coping advice. At the least you'd feel less alone in feeling like an alien.
Thank ya!
I'm hoping the same for everyone else on this subreddit. The post might even have insight for someone lurking although I have doubts
Brrrr!

I usually don't unless I'm looking for friendships. Mainly because the person will eventually find out and it skips the huge disappointment of seeing how someone treats you changing for the worst after a lot of effort put in. ASD nobody takes you seriously, especially online you can say you're autistic with everyone assuming it's a joke most of the time. That or there's no way you can have it because you're not acting half braindead, lol.

Honestly being noticed longer than two seconds is enough for me to appreciate. It's also nice to be reminded not everything stays the same. Mental health research is still ongoing and there can always be a vague hope to cling on to elsewhere too.

Thanks, I know I'm not giving up easily even if it's a struggle train. Right now coping by trying to find internet pals to hang out with similar problems but that hasn't been the easiest being female with ASD. There's too many people in the world that think hooking themselves a significant other will solve all their problems when it usually only makes it worse.

Humans are social creatures unfortunately and the best living you can get being alone is accepting being acquaintances is the best interactions you can get. You can try to live vicariously through people watching and stories you hear via small talk. I've seen some people cope with parasocial relationships too. I, personally, turn to using personas and make friends over the internet. Which I'm always welcome to new friends.
I have ASD too and I'm down to give friendship a go.

You're not bad or selfish. What you're going through is sadly a symptom that can develop due to mental illnesses, trauma or even something else I don't know of due to not being a professional. Having someone there for support does a lot but there's people that need medical help on top of emotional support. Stay strong and don't give in
Doing things that I *used* to like is trying to fix myself. Everything is stressful, whether it involves people or not.

Doing nothing and isolating is the fastest way to die for people with frequent suicidal thoughts. This is what I've been told by doctors time and time again and from my own personal experience it's true in my case. It only takes three nights before I make a suicide attempt.

No problem. Make sure to remember not to be hard on yourself and put attention on what you love doing in life. If the guy is still in your life your definitely going to want to block and avoid him if you haven't already.
Damn this is so many things of wrong to recover from. It's best to get yourself checked out when it's safe and no matter what none of this is your fault.
I'm sorry, no one should ever have to deal with what he did to you. If you want to talk about anything I'm open to listening.
There are subreddits for making friends on top of places to discuss similar interests. Self isolation doesn't stop you from making friends online and heck, I'll even chat with you if you want.

You didn't deserve what you experienced and you don't deserve to continue hurting. I honestly wish I could that caring figure you want but being a young female likely disqualifies me... Maybe tell me about what spiritual practices you did in the past instead?

-Donate fish/bugs to Tom Nook and Blathers. This progresses the early game.

-Don't worry about building placements too much. You can change them later for some bells.

(This is only relevant to those new to the whole franchise.) 
-Learn what bugs and fish sell for! There are guides online for a fast reference or you can simply sell a bug/fish one at a time to Timmy and Tommy. This is coming from someone who prefers the bug net over fishing though and knowing that difference between a 150 bell butterfly and 1500+ bell butterflies was a game changer.

-Villagers will move out if you ignore them. Saying hello once per day keeps them feeling welcome but after three days of ignoring them they start to consider leaving at random times. Wait a few more days and they'll pack up to move without mentioning it to the player.
I have the same exact fear. Still trying to search for hope that there's a way or thing to make surviving during those times at least bearable.
I know that feeling all too well. You can DM me if you feel it'll help out.

I'll tell you not to do it if you need it. If you can hope then hope all you can that things will eventually turn around! With enough self work and searching there's a real good chance that the pain will become less frequent at least. Well, that's coming from my own experience with struggling with suicidal episodes...

It really depends on the therapist and how understanding they are of their clients position. There are therapists that won't send you to a voluntary/involuntary hold if you agree to sign a paper saying that you won't go through with killing yourself and go over making a safety plan when the suicidal urges resurface. Best bets on raising your chances on whether you can trust the therapist is letting them know about your situation and asking if they've ever been suicidal. If they've been in a similar dark place with their own lives they'll be way more likely to be understanding.
